body: Looks like this is the same problem: https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs-csi-driver/issues/172
I opened this issue in the main repo, because it might be a problem on how `weed mount` is designed and not the CSI driver itself

I'm pretty sure this is the case, if you increase the sleep after the `fio` finishes the size of all files are correct and you don't see error logs anymore. Part of the problem is metadata inconsistency (which is ok and to be expected), in node of my tests I added a 15m sleep, after all pods finished there were 2 files with `0 bytes`, after a few extra minutes they started reporting the correct size. But when running the test with no sleep or low amount of it, even after hours the files are still in this broken state. Something that contributes with my theory is the fact that the memory usage of the CSI driver grows quite a lot during my tests, this growth might be related to things being cached and flushed with time.

Some more testing and maybe is related to small files (<= 256KiB), running the same test with `1MiB` files doesn't show this problem.

```
[global]
ioengine=libaio
direct=1
thread=1
group_reporting=1
readwrite=write
percentile_list=50:95:99:99.9:99.99
filesize=1M
bs=512K
create_on_open=1
allow_file_create=1

directory=/swfs/target/distributed-write-128-32M-1
rate=1M,8M
numjobs=4
openfiles=16
nrfiles=4096

[write]
```

Ok looks like the problem is related to small files and more than one filer server. If I run the test with a single filer server there are no files with 0 bytes, running the same test with 3 filer servers leads to the problem

Amazing you can create hundreds of mounts to test! What is the actual use case?

For N filers, with leveldb/rocksdb, there is a N*N filer to filer metadata events transmission. Very likely some messages got lost or out of order on different filers.

Do you see any similar problem with N filers but with a shared store, such as redis, database, etc?

About the use case, just testing how SeaweedFS handles a high number of mounting points.
I will test it later using different storage backend and let you know, right now I'm using leveldb

the problem is that is not being eventually consistent, even after days the files still show as 0 bytes. So the data was definitely lost

https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/3729e9ba257fd365aa96aac90fb4a97d69ac69b2/weed/util/log_buffer/log_buffer.go#L18

It seems the buffer for metadata is overwhelmed and flushed to disk too quickly, so some filers missed the metadata events.
I will take a look at this tomorrow, because I will have to build SWFS manually

The issue is that the weed mount is round-robin file creation across multiple filers when they have independent stores:
File Creation: The mount creates file_X on filer1
Content Updates: The mount tries to update file_X on filer2 or filer3
Error: filer2/filer3 don't have file_X in their local store yet (metadata sync delay).

One way to fix this is: the `weed mount` can hash a file to a filer, instead of round robin to each filers.
